reason: The cited evidence (E1–E3) discusses HEA coatings, Mn dissolution in molten salt, and Ti passive layers, but none addresses the native oxide on Q235 steel, its amorphous-to-crystalline transformation, or the effect of annealing on its corrosion resistance. The key premises are therefore unsupported by the provided passages.
premises: Q235 steel has a native amorphous iron oxide passive layer
Amorphous passive films are thermally unstable and transform to non-protective phases at 700–900 °C
Annealing can convert an amorphous oxide to a more crystalline, stable film
Crystalline oxide films provide better high-temperature corrosion protection than amorphous ones
Corrosion of Q235 is controlled primarily by passive film stability, not alloying elements or coatings
